description: Running a Windows Server domain: installation, Active Directory design, accounts, file and print services, Group Policy, DNS and the monitoring that keeps it healthy, all practised on virtual machines. Taught to the depth of the professional Windows Server administration certification.
modelledOn: Microsoft AZ-800 / AZ-801 Administering Windows Server Hybrid Core Infrastructure
Limoncelli, Hogan and Chalup, The Practice of System and Network Administration
Microsoft Learn Windows Server and Active Directory documentation
outcomes: Install and configure Windows Server (Desktop Experience and Server Core) in a virtual lab.
Design and deploy an Active Directory forest with sites, OUs and a security model that fits an organisation.
Manage users, groups, computers and service accounts at scale with the GUI and PowerShell.
Provide file and print services with NTFS and share permissions, quotas, DFS and shadow copies.
Apply Group Policy to configure and secure desktops and servers and troubleshoot its application.
Configure DNS and DHCP for a domain, add server roles, and monitor, back up and recover servers.

units.title: Windows Server introduction and installation
topics: Roles of a server; Windows Server editions, licensing, Desktop Experience versus Server Core
Building a virtual lab: Hyper-V or VirtualBox, networks, snapshots
Installation, initial configuration, naming, static addressing, activation, updates
Server Manager, Windows Admin Center and PowerShell as the three management surfaces
Storage: disks, volumes, Storage Spaces, ReFS versus NTFS

units.title: Active Directory introduction and design
topics: Directory services and LDAP; forests, domains, trees, trusts; the global catalogue
Domain controllers, FSMO roles, replication and sites
Organisational units and delegation; naming standards
Designing AD for a university: faculties, departments, labs, staff and students
Promoting a domain controller and joining computers to the domain

units.title: Active Directory security
topics: Authentication with Kerberos and NTLM; the authentication process
Security principals, SIDs, access tokens, ACLs
Privileged accounts, tiered administration, protected users, least privilege
Password policies, fine-grained password policies, account lockout, MFA options
Auditing logons and changes

units.title: Account management
topics: User accounts, templates, attributes, profiles and home folders
Group types and scopes (domain local, global, universal); AGDLP nesting
Computer accounts, service accounts, managed service accounts
Bulk creation from a CSV with PowerShell; disabling and offboarding

units.title: File and print services
topics: Shared folders, SMB, share and NTFS permissions and how they combine; access-based enumeration
File Server Resource Manager: quotas, file screens, reports
DFS namespaces and replication; shadow copies and previous versions
Print server role, printer deployment via Group Policy, drivers and queues
Offline files and folder redirection

units.title: Group Policy
topics: GPO structure, linking, inheritance, enforcement, blocking, filtering by security group and WMI
Administrative templates, security settings, preferences, software deployment, scripts
Common policies: password, lockout, desktop restrictions, drive mapping, Windows Update
Processing order, loopback, slow links; gpupdate, gpresult and the Resultant Set of Policy
Central store and version control of GPOs

units.title: Windows networking and DNS for Active Directory
topics: TCP/IP configuration, network profiles, Windows Firewall with Advanced Security
DHCP server role: scopes, options, reservations, failover
DNS server role: zones, records, AD-integrated zones, forwarders, root hints, scavenging
SRV records and how clients find domain controllers; troubleshooting with nslookup, dcdiag, repadmin
IPv6 on Windows networks

units.title: Additional AD server roles
topics: Certificate Services (AD CS): enterprise CA, templates, auto-enrolment
Federation Services and Entra ID (Azure AD) hybrid identity in brief
Remote Desktop Services and Web Application Proxy
Windows Server Update Services and Windows Deployment Services

units.title: Server management and monitoring
topics: Event Viewer, Performance Monitor, Resource Monitor, Task Scheduler
Windows Server Backup and Active Directory recovery (authoritative and non-authoritative)
PowerShell remoting and scripting routine tasks; Desired State Configuration in brief
Documentation, change control and disaster recovery planning for a small institution

schedule.title: Windows Server roles and a first installation
schedule.exercise: Compare Desktop Experience and Server Core for a small office server in a short table covering footprint, tools and risk.

tasks.title: List the roles a small office server hosts and choose an edition and installation type for three given organisations, justifying each
Name a server, set a static address, apply updates and verify the configuration with PowerShell commands on a fresh virtual server
Build a virtual lab network with an internal switch, a server and two clients, and check connectivity before and after a snapshot rollback

schedule.title: Management surfaces and storage
schedule.exercise: Write a short note explaining when you would use Server Manager, Windows Admin Center or PowerShell for the same task.

tasks.title: Perform the same task, adding a local user, in the graphical tools and in PowerShell, and compare the steps
Create a volume on a new virtual disk, format it with NTFS, and verify the size and free space with PowerShell
Build a mirrored storage space from three virtual disks, fail one disk and show the data is still readable, then replace the disk

schedule.title: Active Directory structure
schedule.exercise: Draw a forest with two domains and one tree, marking the trust relationships and the global catalogue servers.

tasks.title: Draw and label a single-forest, two-domain AD structure and state what the global catalogue holds
Inspect the FSMO roles and replication partners of a small domain, move one role between two domain controllers and confirm the change
Design organisational units and delegate password reset rights to a help desk group, then test the rights with a delegated account

schedule.title: Designing and building a domain
schedule.exercise: Write an AD naming standard for users, computers and groups for a university and justify each rule.

tasks.title: Promote a virtual server to a domain controller and join a client machine, then verify the join with PowerShell
Create the OU structure for faculties, departments, labs, staff and students and move 20 sample accounts into the right OUs
Redesign a given flat AD of 200 accounts into a delegated OU hierarchy and justify the split between staff, students and service accounts

schedule.title: Authentication, privilege and auditing
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph why a domain administrator should not log on to ordinary workstations.

tasks.title: Trace the Kerberos ticket steps for a user opening a file share and mark the ticket granting ticket and service ticket
Inspect the access token and group SIDs of a signed-in user and explain which permission entries grant or deny access to a folder
Configure a fine-grained password policy and lockout for administrators, then test it with seven wrong password attempts and audit the logon events

schedule.title: Users, groups and bulk administration
schedule.exercise: Draw the AGDLP nesting for a lab folder that students read and lecturers modify.

tasks.title: Create a user from a template with a home folder and profile path, then verify its attributes with PowerShell
Apply AGDLP by placing users in global groups, nesting them in a domain local group and granting that group access to a shared folder
Write a PowerShell script that creates 50 accounts from a CSV, puts them in groups, disables leavers and reports errors from bad rows

schedule.title: File sharing, quotas and DFS
schedule.exercise: Work out the effective permission for a user who has different share and NTFS permissions, and explain the rule used.

tasks.title: Create a shared folder and set share and NTFS permissions so that students read and staff write, then test with two accounts
Apply a quota and a file screen that blocks video files on a student home drive, and generate a usage report
Set up a DFS namespace with two folder targets and replication, then fail one server and confirm users still reach the files

schedule.title: Printing and folder redirection
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page plan for deploying printers to 100 lab computers by Group Policy, covering drivers and queues.

tasks.title: Install a print server role, add a shared printer with a driver and deploy it to a group of clients by policy
Redirect users' Documents folders to a server share and verify that files appear on the server after logging on from another computer
Configure offline files for a laptop user, disconnect from the network, edit a document, reconnect and resolve a sync conflict

schedule.title: Group Policy fundamentals
schedule.exercise: Predict which of three policies applies to a computer in a nested OU and explain the order of processing.

tasks.title: Create a GPO, link it to an OU and verify with a test account that the setting applies
Create GPOs for password rules, desktop restrictions and a drive map, link them correctly and test with a student and a staff account
Deploy software and a logon script by policy to security-group-filtered computers, then test two machines and confirm which receives each setting

schedule.title: Group Policy troubleshooting
schedule.exercise: Write a troubleshooting flow that starts with gpresult output and ends with the cause of a policy not applying.

tasks.title: Run gpupdate and gpresult on a client and read which GPOs applied and which were denied, and why
Predict and verify the outcome of conflicting GPOs with enforcement, blocking and loopback processing on a lab computer
Set up a central store for administrative templates, then diagnose a GPO that does not apply because of a security filtering error

schedule.title: Network services: firewall, DHCP and DNS
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph how a Windows client finds a domain controller using DNS service records.

tasks.title: Configure addressing and firewall rules on a server so that file sharing works but remote desktop is limited to the admin subnet, and test both
Set up a DHCP scope with reservation and options for a lab VLAN, then confirm leases and a failover partner
Diagnose a client that cannot join the domain by checking SRV records with nslookup, running dcdiag and repairing a missing DNS entry

schedule.title: Certificates, identity and updates
schedule.exercise: Draw the sequence of auto-enrolment of a certificate to a domain computer, from template to issued certificate.

tasks.title: Set up an enterprise CA and a template, then enrol a computer and verify the issued certificate in its store
Configure an update server that approves patches for a test group first, then for all computers, and check report status
Plan a hybrid identity for a university with on-premises AD and cloud services, choosing sign-in method and handling an outage in the scenario

schedule.title: Monitoring, recovery and operations
schedule.exercise: Prepare a one-page disaster recovery plan for a small institution, covering what is backed up, how often and who restores it.

tasks.title: Use event logs, performance counters and Task Scheduler to find why a server slows down every night at 02:00
Back up a domain controller, delete an OU, then restore it with an authoritative restore and confirm users reappear
Write a PowerShell script that checks disk space and failed logons on three servers remotely and emails a report, then test failure handling
